key: Let not this fetter bind us fast: may he release us for success; For strong is Indra and renowned.
s: In a hymn to the Adityas and Aditi, pleading for life and release, the verse turns for once to Indra; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 8.56.8, reads the fetter as a binding net and Indra, controller of all, as keeping the speakers clear of it.

evidence.gloss: Let not the setu, the binding net, bind us; let him keep us clear, away from the net, for a great work. Who? Indra alone, renowned, the controller of all: let him keep us clear.

reason: Second judgement with the refutation in hand. verse.js ok (Rig Veda 8.56.8 at [675,8]); app 8.56 is standard 8.67, and the packet Sanskrit on 8.56.8 (mā naḥ setuḥ siṣed ayam) is this verse. On it Sāyaṇa glosses setu as bandhako jālaḥ (the binding net), parivṛṇaktu as keeping us clear of the net for a great work, and Indra as śrutaḥ, vaśī sarvasya vaśīkartā: the net reading is his own and holds. The refuter is right that the preface clause credited Sāyaṇa with the Anukramaṇī’s list of seers (he opens it with atrānukramaṇikā) and that the clause read awkwardly, and the evidence covered only v8. Rather than rest on the preface, I removed that clause and kept only what his words on 8.56.8 carry: the fetter as a binding net and Indra, controller of all, keeping the speakers clear of it. src narrowed to 8.56.8 (standard 8.67.8). Plain sense unchanged and faithful: Indra is named only in v8 of a hymn to the Adityas, Mitra, Varuna, Aryaman and Aditi asking for life and release. 43 words; entry-check ok.
